questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A bullet of mass 10 g is fired with a speed of 400 m/s from a gun of mass 4 kg. The recoil speed of the gun is:
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved and was initially zero, so 4 × v = 0.010 × 400, giving v = 1 m/s in the opposite direction.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe of length L, compared with an open pipe of the same length, is:
questions.explanation: A closed pipe supports a quarter wavelength in its fundamental and an open pipe half a wavelength, so the closed pipe sounds an octave lower and gives only odd harmonics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A moving coil galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting:
questions.explanation: A shunt carries most of the current and keeps the ammeter's resistance very low, as an ammeter must not disturb the circuit it measures. A voltmeter needs a series high resistance.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 4: Moving Charges and Magnetism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An aqueous solution of sodium acetate is basic because:
options: The acetate ion undergoes hydrolysis to give OH⁻ ions
Sodium ion hydrolyses to give OH⁻ ions
It does not dissociate in water
questions.explanation: The salt of a weak acid and a strong base undergoes anionic hydrolysis: CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O gives CH₃COOH and OH⁻, so pH rises above 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Terminal alkynes such as ethyne are weakly acidic because the hydrogen is attached to a carbon that is:
options: sp hybridised with high s character
questions.explanation: An sp carbon has 50 percent s character, holds the electron pair close to the nucleus and so releases the proton more easily. Acidity follows sp > sp² > sp³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following aqueous solutions is isotonic with human blood and therefore used for intravenous injection?
options: 0.9 percent sodium chloride, that is normal saline
questions.explanation: Normal saline has the same osmotic pressure as blood, so red cells neither swell and burst in a hypotonic fluid nor shrink in a hypertonic one.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In the life cycle of a moss, the dominant, photosynthetic and free living stage is the:
questions.explanation: In bryophytes the gametophyte is the main plant body and the sporophyte stays attached to it and depends on it for nutrition, the reverse of what happens in ferns.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In cyclic photophosphorylation, which of the following is produced?
questions.explanation: Only PS I takes part, the electron returns to the same photosystem, and no water is split, so neither NADPH nor oxygen is formed.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 11: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental chordate character present in all chordates at some stage of life?
questions.explanation: Chordates have a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits. Non-chordates have a ventral solid double nerve cord instead.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the action of a vaccine?
options: It supplies ready-made antibodies to the body
It introduces antigens so that the body makes antibodies and memory cells
It kills all pathogens already present in the body
It replaces the damaged immune cells
questions.explanation: Vaccination gives active immunity: memory B and T cells recognise the real pathogen later and mount a rapid, massive response. Ready-made antibodies would be passive immunisation.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease
